title: P0 hosted API: header mismatch fallback timeline and runbook draft
content:
Summary:

Short: On 2026-12-07 03:12 UTC we observed a P0 affecting Hosted API where a sudden configuration drift in the edge router header normalization logic caused a malformed upstream fallback to be selected. That fallback path returned 5xx errors for streaming connections and increased TTFB for non-streaming requests. Impacted ~8% of active customer sessions for ~42 minutes; elevated 5xx rate peaked at 18% on the streaming path.

Why this is different: usually we see KV-cache or scheduler issues; this incident was an interplay of header canonicalization (X-Forwarded-Proto variants) + an overly permissive fallback selector that matched an internal maintenance pool. The pool had recently been added to routing but not fully health-checked yet.

Timeline (all times UTC):
- 03:09 — First small spike in 5xx rate on streaming edge (alert threshold p1).
- 03:12 — Pager fires (p0 override) after streaming 5xx sustained >10% for 3m and p98 TTFB > 1.2s. On-call (Ethan) acknowledges.
- 03:13 — Slack thread: #sre-incident (SRE-4219) created by pager. Quick triage: streaming+non-streaming both showing elevated errors but streaming worse.
- 03:14 — Checked recent deploys: none to core serving in last 2 hours. Edge config change detected in control plane at 03:08 (auto-propagated).
- 03:15 — Correlation with edge router logs: 'header-normalize' component returned header variants for X-Forwarded-Proto (null vs https) causing fallback selector to prefer maintenance pool 'dedicated-maint-v2' (unhealthy).
- 03:17 — Temporary mitigation: add header normalization rule to force 'https' for all inbound requests at edge (hotfix via control plane). Immediate drop in fallback matches to maintenance pool but 5xx still elevated due to in-flight streaming sessions.
- 03:23 — Began draining maintenance pool and flagged it Out-of-Service (OOS). Non-streaming errors drop to baseline within 4 minutes.
- 03:30 — Streaming sessions continued to see fragmentation and reconnects; we initiated forced session reassign for affected sessions (edge command: session-reassign --filter prefix=streaming-edge-03 --grace=0).
- 03:51 — Metrics stabilized; 5xx < 0.5% and streaming P99 latencies returned to expected window. Incident declared mitigated at 03:55.

Impact:
- Affected customers: estimated 8% of active sessions across hosted-api region us-west-2.
- Symptoms: streaming chunked responses failing (5xx), clients experienced reconnects and partial content loss; non-streaming text generation experienced higher TTFB and sporadic 500 responses.
- Business: transient leaky retries caused some billing anomalies; alerted billing team for reconciliation.

Root cause (working hypothesis):
1) A recent edge config change (auto-propagation) introduced a header-normalize variant that occasionally emitted an empty X-Forwarded-Proto for keepalive TCP-offload paths.
2) The fallback selector logic prioritized pool labels instead of health, and the new 'dedicated-maint-v2' pool lacked robust health-check gating (it was in the system but not fully primed).
3) Streaming code path had weaker session re-assignment semantics on fallback errors: it left half-open sessions that then retried and amplified 5xx by creating reconnect storms.

Evidence supporting hypothesis:
- Control plane audit shows config push at 03:08 with change id cp-20261207-0812 referencing header-normalize feature flag.
- Edge router logs show 'match=fallback:dedicated-maint-v2' correlated with X-Forwarded-Proto=="" entries.
- Pool 'dedicated-maint-v2' instance health reports showed 0/6 healthy until 03:24 when manually OOS'd.
- Session logs show reconnect spikes originating from the same edge shard id range.

Contributing factors:
- Lack of strict health gating for newly created pools; system allowed assignment before health pass.
- Fallback selection uses label precedence over health and age.
- Streaming session lifecycle lacks a fast-path to drop and reassign when fallback responses begin returning 5xx.

Short-term mitigations applied during incident:
- Quick control-plane hotfix to normalize X-Forwarded-Proto to 'https' for all inbound (rolled at 03:17).
- Immediate OOS and drain of 'dedicated-maint-v2' pool (03:23).
- Forced session-reassign for impacted streaming shards (03:30).
- Throttle retry logic at gateway to avoid retry storms (config TTL lowered from 60s to 10s for 1 hour).

Permanent fixes and runbook changes (draft):
1) Routing/Pool gating: ensure any newly created pool must pass >=2 health checks spaced 30s apart before assignment. Owner: Arjun Rao. ETA: 2027-01-15.
2) Fallback selection logic: change priority to health > label age > label precedence. Add telemetry to show when pool selection used a non-healthy flag. Owner: Lena Kim. ETA: 2026-12-20.
3) Header normalization: revert to strict canonicalization for X-Forwarded-* headers and add unit tests that simulate TCP offload paths. Owner: Platform Edge team (Samira Noor). ETA: 2026-12-17.
4) Streaming session resilience: add a fast-fail path that marks sessions as failed after N consecutive fallback 5xx within 30s and triggers immediate reassignment. Owner: Serving Runtime team. ETA: 2027-02-01.
5) Runbook updates: new checklist entries for edge-config pushes (preflight health gate, canary fraction, immediate rollback trigger). Also add a diagnostic playbook for 'header mismatch fallback' with the commands below. Owner: Ethan Chen. ETA: 2026-12-14.

Runbook excerpt (draft commands and checks):
- Quick checks: 
  - curl -I https://edge.us-west-2.redwood.ai -H 'X-Forwarded-Proto: https' and with no header to reproduce.
  - kubectl get pods -n edge -l pool=dedicated-maint-v2 -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.conditions[?(@.type=="Ready")].status}'
  - /infra/edgectl list-fallbacks --shard <shard> --since 10m (shows fallback matches per shard)
- Hotfix rollout: 
  - edgectl set-header-normalize --rule="force-xfp:https" --scope=us-west-2 --dry-run && edgectl apply --force
  - monitor fallback matches metric: metrics.hosted.edge.fallback.match_count{pool="dedicated-maint-v2"}
- Streaming emergency: 
  - edgectl session-reassign --filter shard=<shard-range> --grace=0
  - gatewayctl set retry-ttl=10s --scope=global --temp

On-call notes (raw):
- 03:12 — saw spike, grabbed logs from edge-03 (highly noisy).
- 03:16 — toggled hotfix dry-run then apply. forgot to increment hotfix ID in note; call this cp-hotfix-12.
- 03:27 — found that some clients (old SDK) were sending X-Forwarded-* variants, need to notify SDK team.
- 03:33 — streaming reconverge slower than expected; forced reassign seemed to do the trick. Avoided rolling restart because that would have impacted other pools.
- Learnings: add quick health-check summary endpoint for new pools (curlable) so SREs can verify priming quickly instead of tracing health metrics across infra.

Action items (owner, due):
- Add pre-propagation health gate to pool creation flow. (Arjun Rao, 2027-01-15)
- Update fallback selection algorithm and add an experiment to migrate traffic on health-first basis. (Lena Kim, 2026-12-20)
- Add header-normalize unit/integration tests and block auto-propagation if tests fail. (Samira Noor, 2026-12-17)
- Design streaming fast-fail and reassignment path; write e2e test harness. (Serving Runtime eng, 2027-02-01)
- Update runbook and include the exact edgectl/gatewayctl commands shown above. (Ethan Chen, 2026-12-14)
- Billing reconciliation for retry-charge anomalies. (Finance ops, 2026-12-10)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How many customer SDK versions emit empty X-Forwarded-Proto? (Action: Product analytics to sample 500 requests per minute for 48h)
- Is there a way to atomically change fallback labels so selection won't see an intermediate inconsistent state?
- Should we add a streaming-specific circuit breaker that isolates pools returning 5xx for streaming only?

Appendix: quick logs snippets (redacted):
- edge-03.log [03:12:31] match=fallback:dedicated-maint-v2 xfwd_proto="" session_id=shard-03-87923 status=500
- pool-manager [03:22:45] create_pool:dmeta id=dedicated-maint-v2 instances=6 healthPass=0
- session-proxy [03:29:05] reconnect storm detect shard=03 count=236 delta=120s

Notes for post-incident run: keep this draft for 72h, solicit comments from platform-edge, serving-runtime, and product analytics. After consensus, convert to final postmortem with RCA tags and update Confluence page + link to SRE ticket SRE-4219.

-- Ethan (on-call)
